title: Change Certification Committee & RBAC Matrix for Model Promotion Pipelines
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and operationalize a lightweight Change Certification Committee (CCC) and a detailed RBAC matrix for model promotion pipelines (canary, A/B, shadow) to production. The goal is to ensure consistent, auditable sign-offs, minimal friction for low-risk promotions, and automated enforcement of guardrails (SLO gates, evidence bundles, timeboxed approvals) with integrated audit logging and automated rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: A CCC charter exists that specifies when explicit committee approval is required vs. automated sign-off
An RBAC matrix mapping Redwood roles to promotion permissions (promote:staging, promote:canary, approve:production) is published and enforced by the promotion service
All promotion events (request, approvals, artifacts, final outcome) are recorded in the audit log with immutable evidence bundle links
Auto-rollback rules for canary and A/B flows are codified and wired to the rollout controller; rollbacks are observable and reversible via the Console
Playbook and runbook for escalations and manual overrides are published and tested in a dry-run
tasks: Draft CCC charter: scope, membership, SLAs for review (timeboxed approvals), and decision escalation path
Design RBAC role taxonomy and permission set for promotion operations; include cross-account/delegate patterns for Dedicated/Private customers
Implement promotion-service enforcement hooks to consult RBAC and record evidence bundles (PRs, eval results, eval-ids)
Specify audit-log schema: event types, required fields, retention, and immutability guarantees; integrate with internal SIEM/Logging
Define auto-rollback triggers and thresholds (latency P95 increase >20% vs baseline, error-rate spike >3x, quality regression on eval set >5 pts)
Build Console UI for approval workflows: show evidence bundle, one-click approve/reject, timebox countdown, and audit link
Run two dry-runs with staging->canary and A/B flows; capture gaps and update playbook
Create migration plan for existing open promotions and communicate to stakeholders
approvals_required: Product Manager (owner of feature being promoted)
SRE (attests to reliability and SLO checks)
Security (if model or data changes affect privacy/compliance)
Research/Model Owner (attests to evaluation quality and data provenance)
Change Certification Committee (only for high-impact promotions as defined in charter)
audit_log_requirements: Log every promotion event: request_id, actor, timestamp, source_commit/model-version, evidence_bundle_url, decision, decision_reason, SLA_latency
Persist audit logs to write-once storage with append-only retention for 7 years
Expose audit view in Console and ship to SIEM with alerting for blocked promotions
Evidence bundle must include: evaluation artifacts, PR links, perf dashboards (p95/p99), security signoff if required
rollback_triggers: Canary: observed user-facing error-rate > 1.5% for 5m AND >3x baseline error-rate
Canary: latency P95 increases >20% relative to baseline over a 10m window
A/B: statistically significant quality regression on evaluation set (p < 0.05) or user-sentiment delta > -0.10 over experiment window
Shadow: any privacy or data-leak detection from model outputs triggers immediate halt and investigation
Manual: any approver can trigger emergency rollback with required post-hoc CCC review
notes: Trade-off: fully manual approvals increase safety but slow iteration — charter introduces a risk-tiered approach to reduce friction for low-risk promotions
Decision: use evidence bundles (immutable links) rather than embedding artifacts into workflow to reduce storage duplication
Edge-case: Dedicated/private customers may want local-only audit logs; provide config option but ensure minimum export for enterprise compliance
